Hey Mel, thanks Lou for the tag. Usual disclaimer: I haven't seen your leg so I can't diagnose it over a forum. But morning stiffness, sore to squeeze a few cm up from the heel, warms up then aches at night after a big jump in k's is a pretty common story. Usually it's a cranky tendon from overload rather than anything torn.

Rest or push on: neither, really. Tendons don't love complete rest, but they also don't love 48km. Drop back to whatever volume keeps it settled, cut hills and speed work for now, and build back slowly. Limping round the office after that 6k says that was a bit much for now.

Pain rule: up to about 3/10 during running or exercises is ok, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If it's stiffer or sorer the next morning, you did too much the day before, so back off a notch.

Exercises: heel drops are fine, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence these days.
- Every second day, off a step, straight knee and bent knee
- 3 secs up, 3 secs down
- Start around 3 x 15, then add weight (backpack, or the calf machine at the gym) and drop the reps as it gets stronger
- On bad days, swap them for holds: stand on the sore leg up on your toes and hold 30-45 secs, 4-5 times. These usually settle the pain a bit.

A heel lift short term like Lou said is fine too.

What I'd steer clear of: hard stretching into the burn. A sore tendon is usually compressed and irritated, and stretching it tends to aggravate it rather than help. Cortisone near the Achilles is a no as well. It can feel great for a week or two, but it weakens the tendon and raises the risk of it rupturing. Glad you're not keen on the needle.

Also worth knowing: some antibiotics (the fluoroquinolone group) are linked to tendon problems, including ruptures. If you're ever prescribed one, mention to the GP that you've got a dodgy Achilles.

Get it seen if it's not settling in 3-4 weeks. Any sports physio near you in Bayswater will sort you out.

Get it checked urgently, that same day (GP or ED), if you feel a sudden pop, it feels like someone kicked you in the back of the leg, or you can't push off or go up on your toes. Stop running and the calf work until you've been seen, because that can be a rupture and time matters.

Plenty of time before Rotto, so be patient with it. Good luck!
